target_customer: Individuals and enterprises that need to share online accounts with people and AI agents without sharing passwords; CISOs of companies deploying agents
problem: AI agents need access to online accounts, but sharing passwords is insecure and existing controls do not give fine grained, revocable, auditable access.
business_model: Free consumer password and account manager, planned developer API access and enterprise plan
product_category: Identity and access security for AI agents

founders.name: Vivek Nair
prior_employers: CIA (cyber officer and technical lead for cyber units)
US Department of Defense cyber units
education: UC Berkeley, PhD in computer science
founders.background_notes: YC page lists NSF, NPSC and Hertz fellowships and a CIA Exceptional Performance Award.

founders.name: Colin Roberts
founders.background_notes: Press describes him as a cryptographer.

technical_complexity.rationale: Applied cryptography with client side encryption, post quantum key derivation and revocable checkpoint links requires specialist skills that the PhD founders have.

defensibility.rationale: Patented technology is claimed (no patent details found) and credentials stored in the product create lock-in, but identity incumbents are moving into agent identity.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Okta and CyberArk shipped agent identity products by late 2025 according to a Cloud Security Alliance note; no acquisition of Multifactor found.

market_need_then: Rapid enterprise adoption of AI agents in 2025 and security concerns about agents using accounts; the company cites CISO demand and early partners in supply chain manufacturing (self reported).

branding.domain_note: Uses the exact .com multifactor.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and concise, headline Stop sharing passwords. Just send a link.

branding.community_and_virality: Open source orientation, public benefit company, GitHub and social channels; Hertz Foundation entrepreneurship award September 2025 per YC page.

brand_strength.rationale: Name is a generic security term shared with MFA products, though the exact .com helps; no press on the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Multifactor is active and announced a $15M seed in December 2025 led by Nexus Venture Partners, soon after Fall 2025. Founders with CIA and NASA cryptography backgrounds and a rising AI agent security need drove a large early raise, while Okta, CyberArk and password managers are the main threat.
notes: Seed confirmed by several outlets (IDTechWire, Pulse 2.0, Webull) and the company site lists Y Combinator, Nexus, Pioneer Fund and Flex Capital as backers. CB Insights lists $15.5M total and a 2016 founding year, which conflicts and is treated as an error. Total raised beyond the seed is unknown. No dated competitor sources near the batch (the agent identity sources found are from 2026), so the list is empty. Outcome search found no acquisition or shutdown. Name origin not found.
